newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - J&H joins the fray.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - J&H joins the fray.

text.p: Merger and acquisition permutations within the global insurance broking industry have taken on a new complexion with reports that Johnson & Higgins has thrown its hat into the ring.

In all the speculation following Aon's acquisition of Alexander & Alexander in December, J&H was often only mentioned as an afterthought. It ranks among the top broking groups in the world, but is an anomaly because of its partnership structure.

This structure led many observers to the conclusion that an acquisition or merger by or of J&H would be difficult. Now, however, the Wall Street Journal reports that J&H has hired Morgan Stanley to explore its strategic options.
Industry observers believe J&H's attention is currently focused on a deal with Marsh & McLennan, although other names in the frame include AIG and Sedgwick.

Faced with tough market conditions all brokers are under pressure to consolidate. But for Marsh & McLennan there is another reason for possibly snapping up J&H. Acquiring the partnership would restore Marsh & McLennan as the world's biggest broker, a position which it enjoyed for more than 20 years until it was toppled by the Aon/A&A deal.
This year, Marsh & McLennan has already bought French broker CECAR for $200 million and is in talks to acquire London based Minet from St Paul's.
However, these are small fry compared with J&H, whose acquisition would cost around $1.0 billion and would demonstrate Marsh Mac's determination to be the number one global broker.
